issue.title: Port CLIProxyAPI cross-module regression suites (sentinel, built-in tools, parallel calls, disconnect failover, usage logging)
issue.body:
Part of #720 (sub-issue). Case study: [docs/case-studies/issue-720](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/README.md).

Blocked by: #725 #724 #738 (declared with GitHub issue dependencies).

## Summary
CLIProxyAPI's `test/` directory holds cross-module regression suites that encode behaviours clients depend on: Claude Code compatibility sentinel, built-in tools translation, Codex↔Claude parallel function calls, stream-disconnect failover, usage logging, summary/intent translation. Router covers some of these indirectly; porting them makes the coverage explicit.

Blocked by the canonical thinking pipeline, model-level cooldowns, and the translator conformance suite.

Case study: `docs/case-studies/issue-720/test-reuse.md`.

## Proposal
Port each suite as a Router tier-1/2 test with a mock upstream and a controllable clock, keeping the upstream assertions and attributing the source file:
- `claude_code_compatibility_sentinel_test.go` → extend the Claude Code feature matrix (#675)
- `builtin_tools_translation_test.go`, `codex_claude_parallel_function_calls_test.go`, `summary_intent_translation_test.go` → bridge tests
- `codex_stream_disconnect_failover_test.go` → pool failover tests
- `usage_logging_test.go` → usage attribution tests

## Tests
The ported suites; each must fail against a deliberately broken bridge to prove it bites.

## Prior art
CLIProxyAPI `test/*.go` (9 files).

issue.title: docs: case study and sub-issue plan for CLIProxyAPI feature parity (#720)
issue.body:
Issue #720 asks for a deep analysis of CLIProxyAPI, a case study under `docs/case-studies/issue-720`, a list of every requirement with solution plans, a survey of existing components, reuse of as many upstream tests as possible, and sub-issues with GitHub blockers that deliver the work. This PR delivers the analysis and the issue breakdown; the code lands through the sub-issues.

### Case study

[docs/case-studies/issue-720/](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/README.md) compares CLIProxyAPI v8.0.20 (commit `0f96f568`, 918 test files) with Router v1.18.3:

- [README.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/README.md): scope, snapshot, gap summary, reliability/security/safety analysis, issue plan.
- [requirements.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/requirements.md): 15 requirements traced from the issue text plus 4 implicit repository requirements, each with a solution and a verification.
- [feature-matrix.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/feature-matrix.md): ~110 rows across protocol surfaces, providers, routing, thinking, management, platform and tests, each with a Have/Partial/Gap/Skip verdict and the sub-issue that closes it.
- [online-research.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/online-research.md): releases v8.0.11–v8.0.20, documentation mirrors (routing, advanced configuration, management API security), cliproxy-rs, the management center, and ~30 ecosystem tools.
- [components-survey.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/components-survey.md): crates already in `Cargo.toml` and candidates per gap area, with decisions.
- [solution-plans.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/solution-plans.md): options, chosen plan, tests and security notes per sub-issue, plus an out-of-scope table with reasons.
- [test-reuse.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1/docs/case-studies/issue-720/test-reuse.md): which upstream suites to port as vectors, scenarios or intent, and which not to.
- `raw/`: verbatim MIT-licensed upstream documents (README, config example, management API v8, AGENTS.md, LICENSE), extracted route list and test inventory, and the issue JSON.

### Sub-issues and blockers

Twenty sub-issues (#722–#741) are attached to #720 through the sub-issue API; 21 dependency edges are declared with GitHub `blocked_by`. First wave (unblocked): #722 management hardening, #723 per-credential routing policy, #724 model-level cooldowns and retry budgets, #725 canonical thinking pipeline, #726 provider onboarding contract, #727 catalog sources. The dependency table is in README § 6. Closed issues #668–#684 are referenced, not duplicated; open #718/#719 block the observability issue #728.

### Security and safety decisions recorded

Fingerprint "cloaking" and dynamic-library plugins are out of scope; management hardening (#722) blocks the configuration CRUD (#730) and credential lifecycle (#731) issues; configuration reads redact secrets by default; header passthrough is allow-list only; Router's upstream timeout policy from #669 is kept.

### Validation

`rust-script scripts/check-terminology.rs`, `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs` and `cargo fmt --check` pass locally. The change is documentation only, plus a patch changelog fragment. The latest default branch is included.

Part of #720. The parent stays open as the tracking issue for #722–#741.

issue.title: feat: add model-aware cooldowns and live routing controls
issue.body:
Ordinary quota responses now cool the requested `(account, model)` pair, so a `gpt-5` rate limit leaves `gpt-5-mini` available on that account. Terminal quota codes and authentication failures cool the whole account. Vendor utilization windows and pauses retain their account-wide scope.

Closes #724.

- Add bounded retry rounds, credential caps, cooldown waits and a maximum observed cooldown through environment variables and CLI flags. Defaults retain one-round failover, strict pins and upstream timeouts. Requests are never replayed after output starts.
- Observe SSE and Codex WebSocket quota errors, retry empty or interrupted streams before output, and report incomplete streams after output starts.
- Add authenticated, audited runtime strategy changes and pool/account/model cooldown resets. Both endpoints follow management access restrictions and shared authentication lockouts. Resets preserve pauses, usage, credentials and session bindings.
- Add configurable parent-session affinity, correct programmatic CLI defaults and explicit `false` support in JavaScript/Python bindings. Publish regenerated contracts and a minor-release changelog fragment.

The branch merges main through its v1.24.0 release, including configurable catalog sources, account policies, admin observability and canonical thinking controls. Published route IDs stay intact: `ModelDefinitions = 102`, with the new `Routing = 103` and `CooldownReset = 104` appended afterward. Compatibility tests check numeric values and ordering. The catalog entry retains its published inventory position, and all 62 operations and 235 HTTP routes remain available. Weighted routing, exact token grants, aliases, prefixes, exclusions, isolated upstream clients and `disable_cooling`/`relay` rules remain supported.

Policy dispatch shares the retry budget, initial cooldown waits, explicit account attempt limits and response inspection. Regression tests verify active-account attribution and opt-in error captures during failover. Two thinking interactions were reproduced before their fixes: suffix changes bypassed the base model's cooldown, and same-account retry rounds removed encrypted history. Recognized suffixes now share the base model's routing identity; retry preparation strips account-bound history only on an account switch and revalidates the original thinking controls on every retry.

To reproduce the original issue, return an ordinary quota for `gpt-5` on a selected account, then request `gpt-5-mini` on that account: the sibling was incorrectly excluded. Recorded three-account fixtures cover ordinary/terminal HTTP, SSE and WebSocket quotas, the four disconnect cases, retry limits, strict pins, parent affinity, live controls, authorization and auditing. Injected clocks verify expiration; property tests bound arbitrary reset hints. Commands and fixture provenance are in `experiments/issue-724/README.md` and `tests/fixtures/vendor/openai_responses/README.md`.

```sh
cargo test --locked --all-features --test accounts_routing_policy_test \
  --test pool_failover_test --test management_security_test \
  --test network_security_audit_test --test thinking_account_policy_test
```

The initial cooldown-wait regression opts into an advancing request clock. It starts each request at an injected Unix timestamp and advances that scoped clock using elapsed Tokio time on every request poll. The cooldown therefore expires during the retry sleep without depending on a tracing callback. This removes the fixture's reproducible missing-event failure while retaining its one-call assertion, five-second deadline and expired-cooldown counterpart. Deliberately removing the initial round handoff fails with two upstream calls. Twenty complete four-thread repetitions of the advancing-clock implementation pass all 1,020 tests; after introducing explicit clock variants, five rebuilt full-suite repetitions with 32 threads pass another 255. Reusable mutation and bounded parallel probes are in `experiments/issue-724/`. Default-off retry diagnostics explain why a further round is unavailable.

Complete local validation of `ac061bf` passes 971 integration/bin tests across 128 suites, 15 doctests, examples and all 2,199 distinct library tests across sixteen partitions. The local library inventory exactly matches normal Linux CI and retains all 2,183 previously enabled tests. The largest library child RSS is 2,255,348 KiB, below the unchanged 2,350 MiB guard. Exact current-binary contracts/bindings, published compatibility, Node/Bun/Python (ten tests each), TypeScript, strict production/integration/example/benchmark Clippy and repository policy checks pass. The existing ignored soak is exercised by the separate passing Linux/macOS soak workflow.

The final-commit instrumented report covers 80,590 of 92,498 lines (87.13%). The unchanged checker accepts the committed measured baseline of 87.129419% without altering the file; all eight checker tests pass. Coverage floor, ratchet and baseline-review gates pass with no exception. All seven final-commit workflows pass: [CI/CD](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/38015862000), [downstream operations and contracts](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/38015861997), [Docker runtime](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/38015861987), [real-client capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/38015861985), [Linux/macOS soak](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/38015862017), [benchmarks](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/38015862028) and [fuzz](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/38015862021). CI/CD includes passing Linux/macOS/Windows tests, strict lint, coverage and the release package build.

The two CI image builders use Docker's documented `mirror.gcr.io` registry-cache configuration after reproducing Docker Hub's unauthenticated pull limit. The finite manifest probe verifies all four cached hashes against the existing Dockerfile pins. Both image workflows pass on the merged source, including shipped commands, DNS/relay checks and tunnel smoke assertions. Image pins and release-publishing behavior remain intact.

Rust API compatibility: the defaultable `AccountRouterOptions`, `PoolPolicy`, `PoolArgs` and `RoutingContext` structs have new settings. Complete downstream struct literals need the added fields or `..Default::default()`. This minor-release source-compatibility exception is documented in `docs/integration/compatibility.md`; the field-addition lint remains enabled at the minor level and other checks remain in place. Published enum numeric values and ordering are preserved.

issue.title: Kill recovery runs the Telegram alias as the program (sh: /codex: not found, exit 127), then reports the task as oom-killed

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, 193 GB disk, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store (`overlayfs` snapshotter), live-restore disabled. Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot`; tasks run as `$ --isolated docker` containers from `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`. hive-mind 2.34.0, start-command 0.35.4.

At 12:11:39 UTC the kernel OOM-killed the **host dockerd** (7.3 GB RSS, caused by ~22 concurrent `docker diff` calls from a disk-cleanup tool test suite run inside the root container — link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22). systemd restarted dockerd, which SIGKILLed every running container (exit 137): the root `hive-mind` container and four `/codex` solve tasks for link-assistant/router#724, #725, #727, #728. The root container was started again manually at 13:31 UTC; the bot then ran its built-in kill recovery.

## Problem

In-place kill recovery (`$ --resume <execution> -- <command>`) runs the **Telegram command alias as the shell program**. Every recovered `/codex` task fails instantly with exit 127, and the bot then reports it as `oom-killed` and stops tracking it.

```
$ docker logs eec34a2b-aa97-4bf1-8879-b483ab13d784-resume-1
[dind-entrypoint] Starting dockerd (storage-driver=fuse-overlayfs, data-root=/var/lib/docker)
[dind-entrypoint] dockerd is ready after 1s
[dind-entrypoint] image preload/passthrough complete
sh: 1: /codex: not found

$ docker inspect -f '{{json .Config.Cmd}}' eec34a2b-aa97-4bf1-8879-b483ab13d784-resume-1
["sh","-c","/codex https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/728 --think xhigh --auto-merge --tool codex --attach-logs --verbose --no-tool-check --disable-report-issue --language en --resume 01a1200a-276e-76b2-9674-c219f0f54121"]
```

The same happened to router#724 (`9243e682-…-resume-1`, exit 127). Each of these attempts first spent 10–35 minutes and 11–24 GB of disk on `docker commit` of the killed container, only to run a command that cannot exist.

Bot log afterwards (wrong status, session dropped):
```
EVENT session_completion_notified {"sessionName":"eec34a2b-aa97-4bf1-8879-b483ab13d784","exitCode":137,"status":"oom-killed",...}
[VERBOSE] Session eec34a2b-aa97-4bf1-8879-b483ab13d784 removed from tracking (exit: 137, status: oom-killed)
```
The resumed container exited **127**, not 137, but the record kept the old `OOMKilled=true`/137 diagnosis.

## Root cause

- [`buildResumeCommand`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/session-resume.lib.mjs#L256-L274) uses `/${commandAlias}` as the binary when the task came from a Telegram alias (L263-L264). That string is meant for copy-paste into Telegram (#2109), not for a shell.
- [`resumeKilledSessionInPlace`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/session-kill-resume.in-place.lib.mjs#L197) passes `plan.command.display` as the command `$ --resume` runs inside the container.
- The fresh-run fallback ([session-kill-resume.lib.mjs#L163](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/session-kill-resume.lib.mjs#L163)) uses `sessionInfo.command` + `args`, so it is not affected — only the in-place path is.

## Reproduction

1. `/codex https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n>` in Telegram (docker isolation).
2. `docker kill <task container>` while the tool is running.
3. Wait for the kill recovery: the `<name>-resume-1` container exits 127 with `sh: 1: /codex: not found`.

## Expected

The in-place command is the executable (`solve …` / `hive …`) with the original args plus `--resume <last tool session id>`. The alias form stays only in user-facing text. A resumed container's own exit code/reason is reported (127, "command not found"), not the killed predecessor's.

## Workaround (verified)

Re-run the resume with the real program; the snapshot already exists, so this is cheap:
```
$ --resume deb9c2e9-8234-43ef-9648-e102f5d34ebd --output-format json -- \
  solve https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/728 --think xhigh --auto-merge --tool codex \
  --attach-logs --verbose --no-tool-check --disable-report-issue --language en \
  --resume 01a1200a-276e-76b2-9674-c219f0f54121
```
Result: `eec34a2b-…-resume-1-resume-2` started, and Codex resumed the original thread (`{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"01a1200a-276e-76b2-9674-c219f0f54121"}`).

## Suggested fix

- Give `buildResumeCommand` separate `display` (alias, for Telegram/PR text) and `shell` (executable) forms, and use the executable form in every place that runs a command (`$ --resume`, `executeWithIsolation`, any `recoveryCommand`).
- Add a test that the in-place resume command never starts with `/`.
- When a resumed container exits, classify it from its own exit (127 → "command not found", not `oom-killed`) and keep tracking/recovering instead of dropping the session.

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

issue.title: Fresh-run kill recovery cannot resume Codex threads: per-repository CODEX_HOME is not mounted into task containers (no rollout found for thread id)

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, 193 GB disk, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store (`overlayfs` snapshotter), live-restore disabled. Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot`; tasks run as `$ --isolated docker` containers from `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`. hive-mind 2.34.0, start-command 0.35.4.

At 12:11:39 UTC the kernel OOM-killed the **host dockerd** (7.3 GB RSS, caused by ~22 concurrent `docker diff` calls from a disk-cleanup tool test suite run inside the root container — link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22). systemd restarted dockerd, which SIGKILLed every running container (exit 137): the root `hive-mind` container and four `/codex` solve tasks for link-assistant/router#724, #725, #727, #728. The root container was started again manually at 13:31 UTC; the bot then ran its built-in kill recovery.

## Problem

When in-place recovery is not possible, the fresh-run fallback launches `solve … --resume <codex thread id>` in a **new** task container. For Codex that can never work: the thread's rollout is stored in the killed container's own filesystem, so the new run fails within a minute and posts a failure on the PR.

router#727, fallback session `78dcf29e-8ee2-40f5-aca5-2e967ac692af` (comments https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/752#issuecomment-6082862406 and https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/752#issuecomment-6082869911):
```
Warning: Session log for 01a11f62-7b6a-7443-b4e1-c66d343b6915 not found, but continuing with resume attempt
Creating temporary directory for resumed session: /tmp/gh-issue-solver-resume-01a11f62-…
(export CODEX_HOME=/home/box/.codex/hive-mind/repositories/link-assistant/router; … codex exec resume "01a11f62-7b6a-7443-b4e1-c66d343b6915" …)
Error: thread/resume: thread/resume failed: no rollout found for thread id 01a11f62-7b6a-7443-b4e1-c66d343b6915 (code -32600)
❌ CODEX execution failed
```

The same task resumed **in place** (snapshot of the killed container, router#728) found its thread: `{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"01a1200a-276e-76b2-9674-c219f0f54121"}`.

A second fallback (router#725, `f648b389-…`) did not even start: `❌ Insufficient disk space on this host (10215MB available, 10240MB required) — the issue itself was not attempted` (exit 75), and it still consumed recovery attempt 1/3.

## Root cause

- solve runs Codex with a per-repository `CODEX_HOME` built by [`buildCodexCapabilityStatePath`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/codex-capability-preflight.lib.mjs#L162-L164): `~/.codex/hive-mind/repositories/<owner>/<repo>`. Rollouts for the thread are written there.
- Task containers only bind-mount `~/.codex/auth.json` and `~/.codex/sessions` (from `$ --list`: `"volumes": ["/home/box/.config/gh:…", "/home/box/.gitconfig:…", "/home/box/.codex/auth.json:…", "/home/box/.codex/sessions:…"]`), so the per-repository home dies with the container.
- [`startKillRecoverySession`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/session-kill-resume.lib.mjs#L163) launches the fresh run with `plan.command.args`, which always include `--resume <id>`.

## Expected

A fresh recovery run either has the thread available or does not ask for it.

## Suggested fix

1. Before the fresh launch, copy the thread's rollout out of the stopped container (`docker cp <killed>:<CODEX_HOME> …` works on stopped containers) and make it available to the new container (mount or copy into its `CODEX_HOME`), or persist the per-repository `CODEX_HOME` on a mounted volume in the first place.
2. If the rollout cannot be recovered, launch without `--resume` (`--auto-continue` on the existing PR) instead of a run that is guaranteed to fail.
3. A launch refused by the disk preflight (exit 75, nothing attempted) should not count as a recovery attempt and should be retried when space frees up.
4. Check the same for every tool with `--resume` (claude, agent, gemini, qwen): where does each keep its session, and is it mounted into task containers?

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

issue.title: In-place kill recovery commits whole task writable layers concurrently, filling the disk (ENOSPC) and loading CPU for 30+ minutes

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, 193 GB disk, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store (`overlayfs` snapshotter), live-restore disabled. Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot`; tasks run as `$ --isolated docker` containers from `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`. hive-mind 2.34.0, start-command 0.35.4.

At 12:11:39 UTC the kernel OOM-killed the **host dockerd** (7.3 GB RSS, caused by ~22 concurrent `docker diff` calls from a disk-cleanup tool test suite run inside the root container — link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22). systemd restarted dockerd, which SIGKILLed every running container (exit 137): the root `hive-mind` container and four `/codex` solve tasks for link-assistant/router#724, #725, #727, #728. The root container was started again manually at 13:31 UTC; the bot then ran its built-in kill recovery.

## Problem

After a host-wide kill, the bot recovers every killed session in place at about the same time (random delays of 34–73 s, #2498). Each in-place recovery is `$ --resume` in `docker-snapshot` mode, i.e. `docker commit` of the **whole writable layer** of the killed task container. With four Rust tasks that was 11 + 21.2 + 23.5 + 36.8 GiB, almost all of it Cargo `target/` directories (8.6 + 18 + 17 + 31 GB), on a host with 52 GB free.

Observed:
- 4 commits ran concurrently; containerd used ~280 % CPU for 30+ minutes, compressing layers.
- Free disk went 52 GB → 2 GB; the host reached 96 % used.
- router#727's commit failed: `failed to apply diff: write /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/7124/fs/tmp/gh-issue-solver-1791515915848/target/debug/deps/link_assistant_router-…: no space left on device`; router#725's commit failed the same way. Both fell back to fresh runs that failed (#2888).
- Every successful snapshot is a full copy: the original container (11 / 23.5 GiB) and the `start-command-resume/<name>:1` image (46.7 / 62.7 GB including the base) coexist until someone removes the original by hand.
- Even a ~560 KiB layer takes 10+ minutes to commit: with the containerd image store, commit computes the diff by walking the full mounted filesystem.

## Expected

Recovery never fills the disk it needs to keep working, and does not duplicate tens of GB of regenerable build output.

## Suggested fix

- **Avoid the copy:** make the task container resumable with `docker start` (`ResumeMode.DOCKER_START`, no commit). For example, have the launch command read the command to run from a file in the container (written by the bot before `docker start`), so the same container can re-run with `--resume <id>`. Today `docker start` would re-run the gate loop `while [ ! -e "$gate" ]` for a gate file that was already deleted and hang.
- **If a snapshot is needed:** preflight free disk against the container's writable-layer size (with headroom for the compressed blob plus the unpacked snapshot), run snapshots **one at a time**, and drop regenerable caches first (Cargo `target/`, `node_modules/.cache`, …) or exclude them.
- After a snapshot-derived container starts successfully, remove the original stopped container (its data is in the image) and remove obsolete `start-command-resume/*` images after the task finishes.
- Report the state in Telegram (`waiting for disk`, `snapshotting 12/37 GiB`) instead of failing silently.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, 193 GB disk, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store (`overlayfs` snapshotter), live-restore disabled. Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot`; tasks run as `$ --isolated docker` containers from `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`. hive-mind 2.34.0, start-command 0.35.4.

issue.title: Kill recovery notices are posted to the wrong pull request (first linked PR, e.g. the parent plan PR)

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, 193 GB disk, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store (`overlayfs` snapshotter), live-restore disabled. Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot`; tasks run as `$ --isolated docker` containers from `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`. hive-mind 2.34.0, start-command 0.35.4.

At 12:11:39 UTC the kernel OOM-killed the **host dockerd** (7.3 GB RSS, caused by ~22 concurrent `docker diff` calls from a disk-cleanup tool test suite run inside the root container — link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22). systemd restarted dockerd, which SIGKILLed every running container (exit 137): the root `hive-mind` container and four `/codex` solve tasks for link-assistant/router#724, #725, #727, #728. The root container was started again manually at 13:31 UTC; the bot then ran its built-in kill recovery.

## Problem

The kill-recovery lifecycle notices for four different tasks were all posted to **link-assistant/router#721**, an unrelated PR, instead of each task's own PR:

| Task | Own PR | Notice posted to |
|---|---|---|
| router#724 | #749 (`issue-724-878028a21e67`) | https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/721#issuecomment-6081947908 |
| router#725 | #750 (`issue-725-052105988e50`) | https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/721#issuecomment-6081957476 |
| router#727 | #752 (`issue-727-61ea612f008e`) | https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/721#issuecomment-6081964840 |
| router#728 | #753 (`issue-728-9679a13cda3c`) | https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/721#issuecomment-6081974137 |

#721 is the case-study PR for issue #720 (`issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1`), which plans those sub-issues.

## Root cause

GitHub links **both** PRs to each sub-issue:
```
gh api graphql … issue(number:724){ closedByPullRequestsReferences … }
→ [{number:721, headRefName:"issue-720-99e7abc4e6c1"}, {number:749, headRefName:"issue-724-878028a21e67"}]
```
[`resolvePullRequestUrlForSession`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/session-monitor.lib.mjs#L1076-L1110) returns `linkedPRs[0].url` without checking which PR belongs to the session. The session log fallback ([`resolvePullRequestUrlFromSessionLog`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/session-monitor.lib.mjs#L358-L377)) returns the first `/pull/N` URL it meets, so it can pick a PR the agent merely mentioned.

## Suggested fix

- Prefer the PR the session itself created/used: the branch `issue-<n>-*` solve printed, or the PR URL from solve's structured output, stored in `sessionInfo` when the session starts.
- Among linked PRs, pick the one whose head branch matches `issue-<n>-`; never a PR whose branch belongs to another issue.
- Apply the same selection everywhere a PR is resolved for a session (completion messages, kill notices, log attachments).

issue.title: Containers killed by a Docker daemon restart are reported as OOM-killed

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, 193 GB disk, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store (`overlayfs` snapshotter), live-restore disabled. Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot`; tasks run as `$ --isolated docker` containers from `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`. hive-mind 2.34.0, start-command 0.35.4.

At 12:11:39 UTC the kernel OOM-killed the **host dockerd** (7.3 GB RSS, caused by ~22 concurrent `docker diff` calls from a disk-cleanup tool test suite run inside the root container — link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22). systemd restarted dockerd, which SIGKILLed every running container (exit 137): the root `hive-mind` container and four `/codex` solve tasks for link-assistant/router#724, #725, #727, #728. The root container was started again manually at 13:31 UTC; the bot then ran its built-in kill recovery.

## Problem

Containers that were killed because the **Docker daemon restarted** are reported as out-of-memory kills:

```
$ --list → "exitCode": 137, "oomKilled": true,
           "exitReason": "memory-exhaustion (cgroup-oom-killer)",
           "memoryExhaustedReason": "Docker reported State.OOMKilled=true"
bot      → EVENT session_completed {"sessionName":"…","exitCode":137,"status":"oom-killed"}
```

What actually happened (host journal, times CEST):
```
14:11:39 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 823 (dockerd) total-vm:13940936kB, anon-rss:7302520kB …   ← global OOM, not a container cgroup
14:11:41 systemd: docker.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
14:11:45 dockerd: Loading containers: start.
14:11:55 dockerd: Container failed to exit within 10s of signal 15 - using the force container=8bde925c…
```
Earlier that day each task container had a few cgroup OOM kills of a **child** process (`rustc`/`clippy-driver` hitting the container's 2.9 GiB limit: 724 ×5, 725 ×3, 727 ×2, 728 ×2) that the container survived. Docker's `State.OOMKilled` is set once *any* OOM kill happened during the container's lifetime, so it stayed `true`; the exit 137 itself came from dockerd force-killing the containers while restoring after its own crash. hive-mind and start-command read `OOMKilled=true` + 137 as "the container was OOM-killed". The root container (no OOM events, `OOMKilled=false`) was killed the same way at the same second.

The wrong diagnosis has consequences: Telegram and PR text say the task ran out of memory, and it steers any memory-based policy (smaller limits, refusing to resume).

## Suggested fix

- Before reporting `oom-killed`, check that the OOM kill hit the container's main process near `FinishedAt` (kernel journal `oom-kill:… task_memcg=…<container id>` with the init/solve pid, or `memory.events` changing at exit), not an earlier child-process kill the container survived. Detect a daemon restart (dockerd start time later than the container's `FinishedAt`, or many containers finished in the same second) and report it as "killed by Docker daemon restart (dockerd was OOM-killed / restarted)".
- Report the upstream part to link-foundation/start for `$ --list`'s `exitReason`.
- Docs: recommend `"live-restore": true` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json` for hosts running hive-mind, so a dockerd crash or upgrade no longer kills the root container and every task (it would have prevented this whole incident).

issue.title: JavaScript-first Router with full Rust parity via meta-language translation; bulk sub-agent drafting with one CI/CD push gate; Rust CI/CD starts only after JavaScript CI/CD passes
issue.body:
## Goal

Make Router development fast and light on the machines that run it:

1. **JavaScript first.** Every feature is implemented and tested in JavaScript first, and the Rust code is produced from it by automated translation through [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language).
2. **Router gets a native JavaScript implementation with full feature parity** with the Rust one, enforced in CI like meta-language's parity gate. Today `packages/javascript` (`@link-assistant/router`) is a wrapper that runs the Rust binary (`ROUTER_BIN`), not an implementation.
3. **Bulk changes with sub-agents, and one push gate.** Several sub-agents draft all requirements in bulk. Exactly **one** sub-agent owns `git push`: it watches CI/CD, drafts the fixes for **all** failures of the last run, and pushes only once they are all drafted.
4. **Rust CI/CD cannot start until JavaScript CI/CD has fully passed.**

**Scope: this is the rule for all big Rust projects, not only Router.** Wherever a project has a lot of Rust code, development is JavaScript first, with a native JavaScript implementation at full parity, Rust produced by meta-language translation, a single CI/CD push gate, and Rust CI/CD gated on green JavaScript CI/CD. Router is where it is set up and proven first. Requirement 8 carries it to the other repositories.

## Evidence 1: latest unfinished pull requests with a lot of Rust

CI runs counted with `gh run list --branch <head>` on 2026-10-10.

| PR | Size | Commits | CI on the branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| link-foundation/meta-language#201 (draft) | +134,131 / −5,667 | 58 | `CI`: **44 runs, 0 green**, 25 failed, **19 cancelled** |
| link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#184 (draft) | +400,307 / −9,680 | 100+ | `issue-183-acceptance` **0/15 green**; `formal-corpus` 5 failed, `tests` 4 failed |
| link-assistant/formal-ai#1188 | +1,410,501 / −200,572 | 100+ | `CI/CD Pipeline` **0/11 green**, `Layered CI` **0/12**, `Coverage` 0/11 (5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 7 failed |
| link-assistant/router#749 (draft, for #724) | +15,086 / −388 | 33 | `CI/CD Pipeline` **3/18 green**, 9 failed, **5 cancelled** |

Pattern: many small pushes, each one starting the whole matrix and cancelling the previous run. Most runs are red or cancelled, so a full green run is rare even after dozens of pushes. The same workflows are re-run for every push while fixes arrive one at a time.

What already works and should be reused:

- **meta-language**: Rust and JavaScript side by side with a data-driven parity gate (`parity/language-features.json` + `js/scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`), run by both `rust.yml` and `js.yml`, so changing one language without the other fails CI. Translation capabilities and boundaries are documented in `docs/four-language-contracts.md` and `docs/translation-rules.md`.
- **relative-meta-logic**: a dedicated `parity` workflow (15/15 green on #184) next to the Rust/JS jobs.
- **formal-ai**: "JS server parity" in #1188, and the associative stack in `docs/associative-tech-stack.md`.

## Evidence 2: what Rust builds cost on the agent host (2026-10-09 incident)

Router tasks (#724, #725, #727, #728), each in a hive-mind task container with a 2.92 GiB memory limit on an 11.7 GB / 6 CPU host:

- `rustc`/`clippy-driver` were OOM-killed inside the containers again and again: #724 ×5, #725 ×3, #727 ×2, #728 ×2 (kernel `Memory cgroup out of memory`). The agents had to write their own workarounds (`experiments/issue-719/bounded-build.py`, `ROUTER_BUILD_RSS_LIMIT_MIB=2450`, `target/local-unit-shards`, a copied `target/debug-initial`).
- `target/` per task: **17–30 GiB** (#724: 21.2 GiB old + 11.5 GiB resumed work dir; #727: 17.2 GiB; #728: 8.6 + 2.2 GiB). One task's writable layer reached 35.7 GiB, almost all of it `target/` and `~/.cargo/registry`. `target/semver-checks` alone was 1 GiB.
- A Rust build kept one task at about 110–135% CPU for hours; #724 (PR #749) has been running for 8+ hours.
- Disk use from these builds made recovery snapshots 46–63 GB per task and contributed to the disk filling up (link-assistant/hive-mind#2889).

Nearly all of that load is local Rust compilation. JavaScript tests need no compile step and a fraction of the memory and disk.

## Requirements

1. **Case study.** Collect the experience of the PRs above, and of the other Rust-heavy repositories (link-foundation/link-cli, link-foundation/links-notation, link-foundation/start, link-assistant/calculator), in `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}`: what made CI green, what caused repeated red/cancelled runs, how parity is enforced, and what translation through meta-language supports today. Turn the results into the rules below.
2. **Native JavaScript Router with full parity.** Implement Router's logic natively in JavaScript (Node 20+ and Bun), not as a wrapper around the binary: configuration, routing, cooldowns, accounts/tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints, CLI and every operation in `docs/integration/operations.md`. Add a parity manifest and checker on the meta-language model (`parity/…json` listing each feature with its JavaScript and Rust implementation and evidence), and shared fixtures/golden tests that both implementations must pass. Keep the existing wrapper package working, or merge it into the native package, without breaking downstream users.
3. **JavaScript first, Rust by translation.** New features and fixes land in JavaScript first, with tests. The Rust code is generated from the JavaScript source through meta-language translation, plus a regenerate-and-diff check, so generated Rust cannot drift.
